# FlutterGuard - full reference

> Security audit any released Flutter app. FlutterGuard is an offline, on-device security audit app for Flutter apps on Android. It reads the release you select and reports what it finds, with grades A, C or F as triage labels. No INTERNET permission, no account, no root, no PC. MIT licensed.
>
> Canonical: https://flutterguard.dev/
> Google Play (in review): https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.flutterguard.app
> Download: https://github.com/anasfik/FlutterGuard/releases/latest
> Source (MIT): https://github.com/anasfik/FlutterGuard
> Privacy: https://gwhyyy.com/privacy/flutterguard
> Contact: work@gwhyyy.com

## What it is

FlutterGuard is an Android app for people who ship Flutter apps and want to see what a release exposes before someone else does. You point it at an installed Flutter app or a single APK. It runs entirely on the phone and turns the static evidence it reads into checks with grades.

The page at https://flutterguard.dev/ states the same thing in three steps:

1. Discover: FlutterGuard lists the Flutter apps installed on this device, or you pick a single APK.
2. Inspect: Read the SDK versions, endpoints and exposed strings inside the release.
3. Report: Save the evidence on the phone and come back to it whenever you need it.

Flutter-aware inspection: a Flutter release carries clues in its compiled library and asset bundle, not just its permissions. FlutterGuard reads these layers alongside SDK versions, embedded endpoints, exposed strings, AI providers, signing information and network policy.

Maintainer: Anas Fikhi, Flutter and Software Engineer.

## Install

- Android 8.0 (API 26) or newer
- Download the APK from https://github.com/anasfik/FlutterGuard/releases/latest and install it
- No account, no root, no PC, no companion service
- Google Play listing (in review): https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.flutterguard.app

## What it reads

1. APK container: entries, sizes, compression, bundled assets, native libraries and ABIs.
2. AndroidManifest: package and version data, SDK levels, permissions, exported activities, services, receivers and providers, cleartext and backup settings, deep links, debug flags.
3. Release contents: hosts, endpoints, URLs, keys and configuration values that shipped inside the APK, plus the SDKs they belong to.
4. libapp.so: strings and symbols inside the AOT machine code. This is the Flutter application binary, compiled ahead of time.
5. Signing data: certificate identity and structural properties of the signature scheme.
6. Route-like strings: candidate screen and route names found as strings in the binary.

## Grades

Each check result carries a grade of A, C or F. The grade is a triage label for that check, so you can decide what to inspect first. A grade is not a security certification and not a statement that an app is safe or unsafe.

## Offline and private

- The app declares no INTERNET permission. Scans run locally without uploads.
- The app or APK you open stays on the device.
- Reports and history live in private app storage.
- A report can leave the device when you explicitly export it and choose a destination.
- Uninstalling FlutterGuard deletes those private reports and history.

## FAQ

### Is FlutterGuard free?

Yes. It is open source under the MIT licence, with no account, no ads and no paid tier.

### Does it need an internet connection?

No. The app has no INTERNET permission, so scans run entirely on the device.

### Which apps can it check?

Flutter apps you own or are authorised to test, either installed on the device or supplied as a single APK.

### Does a finding prove the app is exploitable?

No. Findings are static evidence from the release, not a confirmed exploit.

### Where do updates come from?

Updates and APK releases are published on GitHub, where the APK is available now. The Google Play listing is in review.

## Limits

- Static analysis is evidence, not proof. A finding shows what is present in the release, not that it is exploitable.
- No runtime hooking and no traffic interception. The app does not run the target or observe its network traffic.
- libapp.so is AOT machine code. FlutterGuard reads strings and symbols; it does not decompile Dart source.
- Routes are candidate strings, not a navigation graph.
- AABs are not supported. Convert an AAB to APKs with bundletool first.
- The signature check is structural: it inspects what the APK contains, it does not prove the signer's identity.
- Some ROMs block APK reads, which can prevent or limit a scan.
- Scan only apps you own or have permission to test.
- Uninstalling the app deletes private reports and history.

## Licence and legal

FlutterGuard is MIT licensed. It is a local analysis tool. Use it only on applications you own or are authorised to test. Findings are evidence for your own review and are not an authorisation to test third-party apps or infrastructure.

## Guides

- [Flutter app security: what a release APK exposes](https://flutterguard.dev/flutter-security/): the manifest, endpoint, string, dependency and signing checks that matter in a shipped Flutter app.
- [How to inspect a Flutter APK on Android](https://flutterguard.dev/flutter-apk-inspection/): a phone-first workflow, the desktop commands, and triage rules that avoid false alarms.
- [ProGuard and R8 in Flutter: what they hide](https://flutterguard.dev/proguard-flutter/): Android shrinking versus Dart obfuscation, and what remains readable in libapp.so.
